all_videos_in_window.title: Surfcasting False Albacore, Cape Cod
all_videos_in_window.description:
Here's a few tips for anyone who has "albie fever" but doesn't own a boat or kayak...⁠
⁠
1) Inlets and jetties in Nantucket and Vineyard Sound during September is where I've had the best luck over the years.⁠
⁠
2) If you think the albies are leader shy, try holding your rod tip high so your leader is out of the water, and your lure is skipping across the surface.⁠
⁠
3) Long casting lures like the 3/4oz silver Hard Shell Jig from Monomoy Tackle which I'm using in this video can help reach fish.⁠
⁠
4) Wear Korkers or studded boots! I forgot them when I filmed this video and I'm honestly lucky I didn't fall and hurt myself.⁠
⁠
Catching false albacore from shore on Cape Cod is no easy task, but it can be done. Good luck!⁠
⁠
Tight lines 🎣⁠
⁠
Ryan

The Elizabeth Islands are one of my favorite places to chase false albacore. Functioning as a natural barrier, they separate Buzzards Bay from Vineyard Sound. The archipelago offers a fascinating mix of complete isolation, ultra-wealthy privacy, and raw New England history.⁠
⁠
When conditions align, baitfish will congregate along the islands drawing the albies in. During this trip with @flatlinercharters from September of a few years ago, the albies were feeding on bay anchovies and readily attacking the Dart 110S from Monomoy Tackle.⁠
⁠

⁠

With sunny skies, excellent visibility, and refreshing breezes, we headed out along the shore following reports of whales near the shore. A blow belonging to a second whale was observed in the distance so after spending some time with the first one, we headed out to investigate the second. On our way, one of our volunteers spotted a pod of dolphins to our side, so we changed course to check them out. all_videos.description:
Here's a few tips for anyone who has "albie fever" but doesn't own a boat or kayak...⁠
⁠
1) Inlets and jetties in Nantucket and Vineyard Sound during September is where I've had the best luck over the years.⁠
⁠
2) If you think the albies are leader shy, try holding your rod tip high so your leader is out of the water, and your lure is skipping across the surface.⁠
⁠

⁠
